en: An instrument or device for domestic use, especially in the kitchen.
Specifically, a eating utensil (fork, table knife, or spoon); a piece of flatware or cutlery.

utensil.ety: From Middle English utensyl, from Old French utensile, from Latin ūtēnsilis (“useful, usable”).

ex.ja: その店では、台所用品を扱っている。

ex.en: I want to buy cooking utensils in one lot.
ex.ja: 料理用具を一括して買いたい。

ex.en: Don't forget to bring kitchen utensils such as knives and cooking pots.
ex.ja: 包丁とか鍋とか、台所用品を持参すること。

note.ja: ラテン語 utensilis（使うのに適した）から。uti（使う）。→「（台所）用具・器具」。use と同じ語源。

en: A divine calling to establish one's lifestyle.

Relatively short; shorter than normal, or compared to others.

ex.en: Put the words in parentheses into abbreviated form.
ex.ja: カッコ内の言葉を短縮形にしなさい。

ex.ja: a⨯bはabと略記される。

note.ja: abbreviate（省略する）+ -ed。ad + brevis（短い）。「短くされた」→「省略された」。brief と同じ。

ex.ja: トムには密かに想いを寄せている人がいるって聞いたよ。

en: The act of agitating, or the state of being agitated; the state of being disrupted with violence, or with irregular action; commotion.
A disturbance of personal tranquillity; disturbance of someone's peace of mind; an emotion combining irritation, restlessness and aggrava…

agitation.ety: From French agitation, from Latin agitātiō (“movement, agitation”).

ex.en: He sat down to recover from his agitation.
ex.ja: 彼は興奮を静めるために座った。

ex.ja: 今はフレッドの錯乱が治まって静かに眠っています。

note.ja: agitate（動揺させる）+ -ion。ラテン語 agitare（揺り動かす）、agere。「動揺・扇動」。

en: Able to agree; possible to be agreed.
Pleasant to the senses or the mind; pleasing, satisfying, palatable.
Something pleasing; anything that is agreeable.

agreeable.ety: From Middle English agreable, from Old French agreable. Equivalent to agree + -able.

ex.en: He could make himself agreeable to almost anyone.
ex.ja: 彼はほとんどだれとでも調子を合わせることができた。

ex.en: That is most agreeable to the taste.
ex.ja: それは口当たりがとてもいい。

ex.en: The secretary gave me an agreeable smile.
ex.ja: その秘書は私に愛想よく微笑んだ。

note.ja: agree（同意する）+ -able。「感じのよい・同意する」。

en: Of, or relating to, algebra.
Containing only numbers, letters, and arithmetic operators.

algebraic.ety: Partly from algebra + -ic and partly from French algébraïque.

note.ja: algebra（代数）+ -ic。アラビア語 al-jabr（復元）。

ja: 人工物（artifact の英つづり）

en: UK standard spelling of artifact.

note.ja: ラテン語 arte factum（技で作られたもの）。art、fact と同じ。

en: Boldly self-assured; confident without being aggressive.
Pungent.
An assertion.

assertive.ety: Borrowed from Medieval Latin assertīvus. Synchronically analyzable as assert + -ive.

ex.en: He was assertive by nature.
ex.ja: 彼は生まれつき積極性に乏しかった。

ex.en: Don't be so self-assertive.
ex.ja: そう我をはるな。

note.ja: assert（主張する）+ -ive。「自己主張の強い」。

en: The act of assimilating or the state of being assimilated.
The metabolic conversion of nutrients into tissue.

assimilation.ety: Borrowed from Medieval Latin assimilatio. By surface analysis, assimilate + -ion.

note.ja: as（〜に）+ simil（似た）+ ation。似たものにすること →「同化・吸収」。

en: To increase; to make larger or supplement.
To grow; to increase; to become greater.
In some languages, a prefix *é- (अ- (a-) in Sanskrit, ἐ- (e-) in Greek) indicating a past tense of a verb.
Especially Old Irish, a preverb, usually ro-, used to give a verb a resultative or potential meaning.

augment.ety: From Middle English augmenten, from Middle French augmenter, from Old French augmenter, from Late Latin augmentare (“to increase”), from Latin augmentum (“an increase, growth”), from augere (“to increase”).

note.ja: ラテン語 augmentare（増やす）から。augere（増す）。「増強する」。auction（値を増す売り方）、author と同系。

ex.en: Don't be a backseat driver.
ex.ja: 脇でいろいろ言わないでくれよ。

note.ja: back + seat。「後部座席」→ take a backseat（控えに回る）。

en: A player positioned at or near a base: first baseman, second baseman or third baseman.

ex.en: His normal position is third baseman.
ex.ja: 彼の正位置はサードだ。

ex.en: The first baseman tagged the runner out.
ex.ja: 一塁手は、走ってきた打者にタッチしアウトを取った。

ex.en: The first baseman is the Achilles heel of our team.
ex.ja: ファーストがうちのチームのアキレスけんだ。

note.ja: base（塁）+ man。「塁手」。

Capable of breaking off without damaging the larger structure.
The act of breaking away from something.
A group of riders which has gone ahead of the peloton.

breakaway.ety: From break + away, a deverbal from break away.

ex.ja: のんきな人が変わりやすいものだ。

en: A pictorial representation of someone in which distinguishing features are exaggerated for comic effect.
A grotesque misrepresentation.
Having the characteristics of a caricature, grotesque.
To represent someone in an exaggerated or distorted manner.

caricature.ety: Borrowed from French caricature, from Italian caricatùra, ultimately from Latin carrus, and so not related to character, which is instead ultimately from Ancient Greek χαρακτήρ (kharaktḗr, “type, nature, character”).

note.ja: イタリア語 caricatura（誇張して描くこと）から。caricare（荷を積む・誇張する）。cargo、charge と同じ語源。

en: An inexpensive, disposable box-like container fashioned from either paper, paper with wax-covering (wax paper), or other lightweight mate…

To put in a carton.

carton.ety: Borrowed from French carton, from Italian cartone. Doublet of cartoon.

ex.ja: １パック卵がいるんだ。

ex.en: I need a single carton of eggs.

ex.ja: その子は猫をボール箱の中へ閉じ込めた。

note.ja: フランス語 carton（厚紙）から。イタリア語 cartone、carta（紙）。「紙箱・紙パック」。cartoon と同じ。

en: A branched, often ornate, light fixture suspended from a ceiling.
One lit by candles.

chandelier.ety: Borrowed from French chandelier, from Latin candelabrum, from candela (“a candle”). Doublet of candelabrum. See also candle.

ex.ja: ガラス製のシャンデリアがテーブルの真上に下がっていた。

ex.en: There was a beautiful chandelier hanging from the ceiling.
ex.ja: 天井から美しいシャンデリアが下がっていた。

note.ja: フランス語 chandelier（ろうそく立て）から。chandelle（ろうそく）。candle と同じ語源。

en: A framework, trough, or tube, upon or through which objects are made to slide from a higher to a lower level, or through which water pass…
A waterfall or rapid.
To parachute.

note.ja: フランス語 chute（落下）から。「落ちる通路」→ parachute の短縮。

To form a clot or mass.

ex.ja: 心配すんな。血はすぐ止まるよ。

note.ja: 古英語 clott（塊）から。cloud、clod と同系。「（血の）塊」。

en: Uncritically satisfied with oneself or one's achievements; smug.
Unduly unworried or apathetic with regard to a need or problem.

complacent.ety: Borrowed from Latin complacēns (“very pleasing”), present participle of complacēre (“to please at the same time, be very pleasing”), from com- (“together”) + placēre (“to please”); see please and compare complaisant.

note.ja: com（強く）+ plac（喜ばせる）+ ent。自分を大いに喜ばせている →「自己満足の・のんきな」。

The behaviour exhibited by an animal to attract a mate.

courtship.ety: From court (“demonstration of such respect as is traditionally given at court; attention directed to a person in power; behaviour designed to gain favour; politeness of manner; civility towards someone”) + -ship (suffix forming nouns indicating a property or state of being).

note.ja: court（求愛する）+ -ship。宮廷の作法から「求愛」。

en: To press, force, or drive, particularly in filling, or in thrusting one thing into another; to stuff; to fill to superfluity.
To fill with food to satiety; to stuff.
The act of cramming (forcing or stuffing something).
A warp having more than two threads passing through each dent or split of the reed.

cram.ety: From Middle English crammen, from Old English crammian (“to cram; stuff”), from Proto-West Germanic *krammōn, from Proto-Germanic *krammōną, a secondary verb derived from *krimmaną (“to stuff”), from Proto-Indo-European *ger- (“to assemble; collect; gather”). ex.ja: その少年は衣類を残らず鞄に詰め込んだ。

en: Unwilling to fight; lacking even the rudiments of courage; extremely cowardly.

craven.ety: From Middle English cravant, either borrowed from Old French cravanté (“defeated”), past participle of cravanter (ultimately from Latin crepare), or a modification of creaunt (“defeated”) after craven (“to crave”).

note.ja: 中英語 cravant（打ち負かされた）から。「臆病な」。

note.ja: debilitate（衰弱させる）+ -ing。ラテン語 debilis（弱い）。

A believer in a particular religion or god.

ex.ja: 長い間獲物を追いかけたのでその犬は寝そべってあえいでいた。

ex.en: He was panting to have a go at it.
ex.ja: 彼はそれを試してみたくてうずうずしていた。

ex.en: He panted under a heavy load.
ex.ja: 彼は重荷に喘いだ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 pantaisier（あえぐ）から。ギリシャ語 phantasioun（幻を見る）とされる。「あえぐ」。

en: A state or federal prison for convicted felons; (loosely) a prison.
A priest in the Roman Catholic Church who administers the sacrament of penance.
Of or relating to penance; penitential.
Of or relating to the punishment of criminals.

penitentiary.ety: From Middle English penitentiary, from Medieval Latin pēnitentiārius (“place of penitence”), from Latin paenitentia (“penitence”), term used by the Quakers in Pennsylvania during the 1790s, describing a place for penitents to dwell upon their sins.

note.ja: ラテン語 paenitentia（悔い改め）から。罪を悔い改める場所 →「刑務所」。repent と同じ。

en: Dangerous, full of peril.

perilous.ety: From Middle English perilous, from Old French perilleus, equivalent to peril + -ous, from the noun peril, or from Latin perīculōsus. Doublet of periculous.

note.ja: peril（危険）+ -ous。「危険な」。

en: That teaches applied arts, sciences, technology, engineering and other academic subjects.
A three-year post-secondary vocational training institute, equivalent of community college in the U.S. or TAFE in Australia.

polytechnic.ety: First attested in 1805. From French polytechnique, from the École polytechnique, engineering school founded 1794 in Paris; from Greek πολύτεχνος "skilled in many arts," from πολύς "many" (see poly-) + τέχνη "art" (see technic).

note.ja: ギリシャ語 polys（多くの）+ tekhnē（技術）。「工芸の」→「工科大学」。
